newsitem.title: FRANCE: Balladur wants French style liberalism - Le Monde.
newsitem.headline: Balladur wants French style liberalism - Le Monde.

text.p: France's former Prime Minister Edouard Balladur, eyeing a return to office, said on Tuesday France had to invent its own style of economic liberalism and that he was against "Anglo-Saxon" models.

In an interview with daily Le Monde, Balladur said the French electorate had shown in the first round of voting in a parliamentary election on May 25 they wanted a more dynamic society in order to tackle unemployment but were also attached to a strong French identity.
"This is why I'm not in favour of an 'Anglo-Saxon' liberalism. Our liberalism must allow for protection and solidarity," Balladur was quoted as saying.
"The Socialists and Communists are relying on solutions from the past which they've been following for 10 years. We prefer to bet on liberty finally to bring down unemployment."
Balladur, who is one of candidates to replace outgoing Prime Minister Alain Juppe if the right clings to power after the second round, called for a new, more determined phase of spending cutbacks.
He said they should apply not only to investment, but especially to operating costs at the state, local authority and social benefits levels.
"That's how we will be able to cut taxes and (employers) charges," Balladur said.

Balladur outlined four measures which could help reduce charges employers have to pay the state and boost employment while ruling out the abolishment of the minimum wage, a measure Senate speaker Rene Monory recently called for.

He said one solution would be to find another kind of revenue, possibly based on companies' turnover, or something similar to the CSG, a tax on most income. This would allow employers to reduce their contributions.
While these ideas needed further study with employers and unions, Balladur said he was very attached to further cuts in employers' charges for low wage jobs.
He envisaged abolishing employer charges for those employed at the minimum wage (SMIC) and introducing a gradual reduction in charges for wages up to one and a half times the minimum wage.
Balladur also said he wanted to extend the maximum length of short-term contracts, currently 18 months.

Another measure to help boost employment would be to remove the legal requirement that companies have to have staff delegates or works councils once their workforce reaches a certain size, often a disincentive for small or medium-sized businesses to take on more staff, he said.
